writing.prompt: Explain how a two-locus test cross can provide evidence about linkage.
writing.model: A homozygous recessive tester contributes a fixed allele combination. Offspring classes reveal the heterozygote’s gamete combinations. An excess of parental combinations over recombinants can support linkage, while equal combinations are expected under independent assortment, subject to sampling and model assumptions.
criteria: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities.
Explains the causal relationship or calculation, not just the final result.
Uses the stated evidence and avoids a stronger conclusion than it supports.

writing.prompt: For Ab/aB, identify parental and recombinant combinations and explain why capital-letter grouping is not a valid shortcut.
writing.model: Parental combinations are Ab and aB because those occur on the original homologues. Recombinants are AB and ab. Parental status depends on phase rather than uppercase versus lowercase notation.

videos.title: Linked genes and recombinant offspring — video support
videos.purpose: Identify linked allele arrangements, parental and recombinant combinations, and use a test cross to interpret gamete frequencies.
videos.fallback: Cross a heterozygote with aabb. The tester contributes only ab, so the offspring's phenotype or genotype can reveal the heterozygote's gamete contribution. Under independent assortment, the four combinations are expected in equal proportions. If the heterozygote has AB/ab and the genes are linked, AB and ab gametes often occur more frequently than Ab and aB. The corresponding parental offspring classes are larger, and the recombinant classes smaller. Read the actual counts, not just the presence of four categories. Linked genes can produce all four combinations if crossing over occurs, but the proportions can differ from 1:1:1:1.
videos.availability: Source hyperlink resolved syntactically; external playback not certified.

steps: The stated parental phase is AB/ab, so AB and ab are parental.
Ab and aB are recombinant combinations.

The excess parental classes is consistent with linkage in this model.
The counts do not mean only 18 cells underwent any crossing over anywhere; they concern the two loci being scored.
